meta.topStoryHeadline: June 2026 Black Arts Brief: Loss, Recognition, and Institutional Upheaval
meta.topStorySummary: June brought major losses in Black music and visual art, a remarkable cluster of Tony wins for Black theatre artists, the Juneteenth opening of the Obama Presidential Center with 30 commissioned Black artists, and deepening instability at the Kennedy Center.
executiveSummary: This update refreshes the Happenings calendar for June 28–July 28, with free summer performances, Black theatre openings, jazz programs, literary events, dance festivals, and ongoing exhibitions across New York City.

The month's strongest Soirée picks are Shifters, The Whoopi Monologues, Classical Theatre of Harlem's Othello, SHABAKA / Kokoroko / Omar / Lovie, and Ellington's Black, Brown and Beige at Jazz at Lincoln Center.

The industry brief centers five major June stories: the deaths of Abdullah Ibrahim, Danny Simmons, and Peabo Bryson; the 79th Tony Awards; Njideka Akunyili Crosby's Obama portrait; the Kennedy Center/WNO dispute; and the Schomburg Center's centennial.

events.title: Declaration: Songs of Democracy, Voices of Hope
events.venue: Lincoln Center — Wu Tsai Theater, David Geffen Hall
events.description: Curated by Suzan-Lori Parks. McBride and Nkwelle bring Black musical excellence to a July 4th-adjacent celebration.
events.artistFocus: Christian McBride, Kurt Elling, Ekep Nkwelle

events.title: SHABAKA / Kokoroko / Omar / Lovie
events.address: East 71st St & East Drive, Central Park
events.description: SHABAKA is one of the most significant voices in contemporary Black British jazz. Kokoroko blends Afrobeat, highlife, and jazz. Omar is a UK soul legend. One of the strongest free concerts of the summer. RSVP now.
events.artistFocus: SHABAKA (Shabaka Hutchings), Kokoroko (led by Sheila Maurice-Grey and Onome Edgeworth), Omar

events.title: Othello — Uptown Shakespeare in the Park
events.venue: Classical Theatre of Harlem — Richard Rodgers Amphitheater, Marcus Garvey Park
events.address: 122nd St & Mount Morris Park West, Harlem
events.description: A Black actor in the title role of Othello, in an outdoor Harlem amphitheater, free to all. One of NYC's most beloved summer cultural institutions. A must for Soirée members who have never seen it live.
events.artistFocus: James Udom (Othello), dir. Carl Cofield

events.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026 — Opening Celebration
events.description: The opening celebration for the Studio Museum's annual teen photography program — cohort-led tours, art-making, and frame-making workshops. A grounding, community-anchored event.
events.artistFocus: 17-member teen photography cohort; work alongside James Van Der Zee archive

events.title: Louis Armstrong at 125, America at 250: A Birthday Celebration for Pops
events.description: A birthday celebration for Louis Armstrong at 125. Free, inside the Atrium. Part of Summer for the City, curated with Jazz at Lincoln Center.
events.artistFocus: Louis Armstrong House Museum Big Band, led by trombonist Sam Chess

events.title: Shifters
events.dates: Previews: July 6. Opens: July 15. Runs through August 30.
events.description: North American premiere of a celebrated Black British play. Two young Black people — young, gifted, separated — crashing back into each other's lives years later. Heather Agyepong received an Olivier Award nomination for this role. A small, precise Off-Broadway space. Not to miss.
events.artistFocus: Written by Benedict Lombe; starring Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra; dir. Lynette Linton

events.title: The Whoopi Monologues
events.venue: Lincoln Center Theater — Mitzi E. Newhouse Theater
events.dates: Previews: July 7. Opens: July 13. Runs through August 30.
events.description: Kerry Washington, Kara Young, and Dominique Fishback revive Whoopi Goldberg's landmark 1984 solo show in a new ensemble production. Five Black women on stage, directed by Whitney White. A once-in-a-season event.
events.artistFocus: Kerry Washington, Kara Young, Dominique Fishback, Kecia Lewis, Danielle Pinnock; dir. Whitney White

events.title: Mereba / Mack Keane / Arima Ederra / Halfmoon BK
events.venue: SummerStage — Herbert Von King Park, Brooklyn
events.address: Herbert Von King Park, 770 Myrtle Ave, Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn
events.description: Mereba's sound draws on Atlanta, folk, and progressive R&B. Arima Ederra brings a visionary Afro-futurist sensibility. Presented by Halfmoon BK and COLORSXSTUDIO. Free in the heart of Bed-Stuy. A great evening for members who want live music outside of the usual Lincoln Center circuit.
events.artistFocus: Mereba (Atlanta-born singer-songwriter), Arima Ederra (progressive R&B artist)

events.title: Studio Museum Uptown Fridays
events.venue: Studio Museum in Harlem — Galleries and Rooftop Terrace
events.description: The Studio Museum reopened its doors after years of construction and Uptown Fridays is its signature summer social event. Galleries open, rooftop views of Harlem, DJs, and dancing. The kind of evening Soirée members should be at.
events.artistFocus: DJs Sterling Juan Diaz, BLKshine (Darryl DeAngelo Terrell), Marcus Logan

events.title: MIKE's Young World: Max B / MIKE with The Band of the Century
events.venue: SummerStage — Herbert Von King Park, Brooklyn
events.address: Herbert Von King Park, 770 Myrtle Ave, Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn
events.description: MIKE (Guinean-American rapper and curator) returns to Brooklyn with an event that doubles as a cultural gathering. Max B (a Black Harlem hip-hop legend) headlines. For members tracking the independent Black music scene and what it looks like right now.
events.artistFocus: Max B, MIKE, Thirteendegrees°, ERISTHEPLANET, SALIMATA, Niontay, Black Noi$e

events.title: Brooklyn Museum Summer Jazz: Beareather Reddy
events.description: Beareather Reddy is a Brooklyn-based blues legend, founder of the Brooklyn Blues Society, and a 40-year champion for the blues tradition. Free with admission. Presented in partnership with the Jazz Foundation of America.
events.artistFocus: Beareather Reddy

events.title: Damon Young presents "That's How They Get You: An Unruly Anthology of Black American Humor"
events.description: Damon Young, founder of Very Smart Brothas, launches a new anthology gathering some of the sharpest Black writers working today. A literary event with names Soirée members will recognize, at an accessible indie bookstore venue.
events.artistFocus: Damon Young (editor/author); contributing writers include Hanif Abdurraqib, Mahogany L. Browne, Kiese Laymon, Deesha Philyaw, Roy Wood Jr., Nicola Yoon

events.title: Mavis Staples / Brother Wallace
events.address: East 71st St & East Drive, Central Park
events.price: Free (RSVP required) — presented in association with the Apollo Theater
events.description: Mavis Staples — daughter of Pops Staples, voice of the freedom movement, Rock and Roll Hall of Famer — in Central Park, free, presented with the Apollo Theater. One of the most significant living voices in Black American music. Brother Wallace opens.
events.artistFocus: Mavis Staples (gospel/soul legend); Brother Wallace

events.title: De La Soul / Pete Rock / Hannibal Buress
events.price: Free — presented with Queens Borough President Donovan Richards and Mass Appeal
events.description: De La Soul and Pete Rock are foundational figures in Black American hip-hop culture. Hannibal Buress joins the bill. Free, outdoors, in Queens — a cultural institution on a park stage. For members who want the full breadth of Black music this summer.
events.artistFocus: De La Soul, Pete Rock, Hannibal Buress

events.title: Sisters Uptown Bookstore — Third Thursday Spoken Word and Music
events.venue: Sisters Uptown Bookstore and Cultural Center
events.dates: July 17, 2026 (recurring Third Thursday). Time: evening; confirm with venue.
events.description: Sisters Uptown is one of the last Black woman-owned cultural bookstores in New York City, in its 25th year on Amsterdam Avenue. Third Thursday is their recurring spoken word and music open mic — no features, no lists, just live literary community. $7 suggested. Members should know this space and support it.
events.artistFocus: Open mic; poets, singers, musicians, Harlem community

events.title: 15th Annual New York City Poetry Festival
events.address: Nolan Park, Governors Island (free ferry from Lower Manhattan/Brooklyn Bridge Park)
events.description: A two-day poetry festival on Governors Island, organized in part by The Poetry Society of New York with a stated commitment to marginalized and underrepresented voices. Five stages, open mics, workshops, and book selling — an event that centers the full range of NYC poetic life, with Black poets and literary organizations well represented. Free and worth the ferry.
events.artistFocus: Over 100 poetry organizations and individual poets, representing the full range of NYC's literary community

events.title: Complexions Contemporary Ballet + LaTasha Barnes' The Jazz Continuum
events.address: Rumsey Playfield, East 71st St & East Drive, Central Park
events.description: Complexions, co-founded by Dwight Rhoden and Desmond Richardson, performs a new premiere honoring Billie Holiday and Sarah Vaughn. Paired with LaTasha Barnes' The Jazz Continuum, presented in association with the Joyce Theatre. Free outdoor performance, Central Park.
events.artistFocus: Dwight Rhoden / Desmond Richardson (Complexions); LaTasha Barnes — musical direction by saxophonist Christopher McBride

events.title: Ellington's Greatest Masterpiece: Black, Brown and Beige
events.venue: Jazz at Lincoln Center — Rose Theater
events.address: Rose Theater, Broadway at 60th St, Time Warner Center
events.description: Duke Ellington's 1943 masterpiece, performed by the JALCO in what will be among Wynton Marsalis' final seasons as Artistic Director. Ekep Nkwelle as vocalist. A landmark piece of Black American classical music, rarely performed in full. Pay-what-you-choose, so accessible to any member.
events.artistFocus: The Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra; music direction by trombonist Chris Crenshaw; with vocalist Ekep Nkwelle and violinist Eli Bishop

events.title: Cindy Blackman Santana / Patricia Brennan Septet / Lucía
events.venue: BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn! — Lena Horne Bandshell, Prospect Park
events.description: Cindy Blackman Santana is a celebrated Black jazz drummer whose career spans Miles Davis tributes, jazz fusion, and rock. Free in Prospect Park. The Lena Horne Bandshell is named for a Black musical icon — a fitting stage for a set of this caliber.
events.artistFocus: Cindy Blackman Santana (jazz drummer, composer)

events.title: Brooklyn Museum Summer Jazz: Terrance Simien
events.description: Two-time Grammy Award-winning Terrance Simien brings his intergenerational band and the traditions of Black American zydeco to the Brooklyn Museum lobby. Free with admission. Presented with the Jazz Foundation of America.
events.artistFocus: Terrance Simien and The Zydeco Experience

events.title: BAAND Together Dance Festival
events.address: Lincoln Center Plaza, Broadway at 65th St
events.description: Alvin Ailey and Dance Theatre of Harlem on the same outdoor stage as ABT and NYCB. Six years running, BAAND Together is one of the most accessible and visually extraordinary events in NYC summer dance. July 28 opening night includes a panel discussion. July 31 features a free West African Workshop at 5 PM in the Geffen Hall lobby, led by Ailey Arts in Education.
events.artistFocus: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Dance Theatre of Harlem, Ballet Hispánico, American Ballet Theatre, New York City Ballet

events.title: PHILADANCO!
events.dates: July 29, 30, 31 at 7:30 pm; Aug 1 at 2:00 pm and 7:30 pm; Aug 2 at 2:00 pm. Curtain Chat: July 30.
events.description: PHILADANCO, the legendary Philadelphia-based Black dance company, returns to the Joyce with works by Rennie Harris — set to Philadelphia International Records — Tommie-Waheed Evans, and Thang Dao. From $10. One of the best price-to-quality ratios in NYC summer dance.
events.artistFocus: Rennie Harris, Tommie-Waheed Evans, Thang Dao; performed by PHILADANCO

news.title: 2026 Tony Awards: The complete list of winners
news.summary: Full winners list for the 79th Tony Awards. Multiple Black artists won across acting, direction, choreography, and costume design.
news.detail: One ceremony delivered four historic or significant wins for Black and trans artists across multiple disciplines. Members who follow theatre need the full list in one place.
news.people: Multiple — Joshua Henry, Zhailon Levingston, Omari Wiles, Arturo Lyons, Qween Jean

news.title: Joshua Henry Thanks Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell for 'Black-Don't-Crack Artistic Brilliance' While Accepting Tony Award
news.summary: Henry won Best Actor in a Musical for Coalhouse Walker Jr. in Ragtime and dedicated his win to Black theatrical predecessors Audra McDonald and Brian Stokes Mitchell.
news.detail: Henry's acceptance speech is as culturally significant as the win itself. Members who care about Black theatrical lineage will want to read the speech.
news.people: Joshua Henry; Ragtime; Lincoln Center Theater

news.title: RAGTIME's Joshua Henry Wins 2026 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role in a Musical
news.summary: First Tony win for Henry after four previous nominations. Ragtime at the Vivian Beaumont Theater.
news.detail: Confirms Henry as the leading Black male musical theatre actor of his generation. Industry context for members who follow the business side of theatre.
news.people: Joshua Henry; Lincoln Center Theater

news.title: Ragtime Wins Best Revival of a Musical at the 2026 Tony Awards
news.summary: The revival of Ragtime takes Best Revival of a Musical at the 79th Tony Awards.
news.detail: Ragtime's revival confirmed Broadway's renewed appetite for Black American historical narratives. Members who missed the production should know it won the top revival prize.
news.people: Ragtime; Lincoln Center Theater

news.title: Zhailon Levingston and Bill Rauch Win 2026 Tony for Best Direction of a Musical for Cats: The Jellicle Ball
news.summary: Levingston becomes only the third Black person to win Best Direction of a Musical. In his speech he honored the Black and Brown trans women and gay men who were ballroom's pioneers.
news.detail: A Broadway institution acknowledging ballroom culture's artistic foundations, with a Black director at the podium. This is a Soirée story: ballroom is Black art, and that was said at Radio City Music Hall.
news.people: Zhailon Levingston; Bill Rauch; Cats: The Jellicle Ball
news.suggestedAction: Share; strong Instagram post; BAC episode candidate

news.title: Category is Tag Team Triumph! Zhailon Levingston and Bill Rauch Win Best Direction Tony for Cats: The Jellicle Ball
news.summary: Behind-the-scenes context and director quotes from the win.
news.detail: Gives texture and voice to Levingston's historic win. Additional reading for members who want more than the headline.
news.people: Zhailon Levingston; Bill Rauch

news.title: 'Thank You Ballroom'; Omari Wiles and Arturo Lyons Win Best Choreography at the 2026 Tony Awards for Cats: The Jellicle Ball
news.summary: Ballroom choreography wins Broadway's highest choreography honor. Acceptance speech opened with "Thank you ballroom."
news.detail: Ballroom as choreographic art form recognized at Broadway's highest award level. Members who know ballroom culture will understand exactly what this means.
news.people: Omari Wiles; Arturo Lyons; Cats: The Jellicle Ball

news.title: 2026 Tony Awards: 'CATS: The Jellicle Ball' Costume Designer Qween Jean Made History as First Openly Transgender Person to Win
news.summary: Qween Jean becomes the first openly transgender Tony Award winner, taking Best Costume Design of a Musical for roughly 500 costumes created for Cats: The Jellicle Ball.
news.detail: A historic first for trans representation at the Tonys, rooted in a production centered on Black and Brown ballroom culture. Significant for Soirée members who care about trans artists, fashion, and the intersection of Black culture and Broadway.
news.people: Qween Jean; Cats: The Jellicle Ball

news.title: Qween Jean makes history at 79th Annual Tony Awards
news.summary: Amsterdam News coverage of Qween Jean's historic Tony win, framed for a Black readership.
news.detail: Black press framing of this story carries a different register than mainstream coverage. Soirée should know how this win landed in Black press specifically.
news.people: Qween Jean

news.title: The Big Reveal: First Official Joint Portrait of President and Mrs. Obama Was Made by Artist Njideka Akunyili Crosby
news.summary: The identity of the artist who created the first official joint presidential portrait of Barack and Michelle Obama is revealed: Njideka Akunyili Crosby. The portrait is on permanent display at the Obama Presidential Center, which opened on Juneteenth.
news.detail: The most significant portrait commission in recent American political history went to a Black Nigerian-American woman. Soirée members who collect or follow Black women visual artists will want to know this. It is also a strong market indicator for Akunyili Crosby's trajectory.
news.people: Njideka Akunyili Crosby; Obama Presidential Center
news.suggestedAction: Share; newsletter; BAC episode on Black portraiture

news.title: Obama Presidential Center opens on Juneteenth with largest commissioning of Black artists in American institutional history
news.summary: The Obama Presidential Center opens in Chicago's South Side on Juneteenth with a permanent art program of 30 commissioned works by Black artists. No American institution has launched with this scale of Black artistic commissioning.
news.detail: A new cultural landmark built on Black art and opened on Juneteenth is a structural shift in how presidential legacies can center Black cultural production. The list of 30 artists is a reading list for Soirée members interested in the most important living Black artists working in America.
news.people: 30 commissioned Black artists including Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Rashid Johnson, Lorna Simpson, Carrie Mae Weems, Mark Bradford, Martin Puryear

news.title: Black artists on identity, representation, and Mapplethorpe's legacy
news.summary: Amsterdam News piece on Black artists speaking to questions of identity, representation, and the ongoing conversation around Mapplethorpe's legacy and his photographing of Black men.
news.detail: The Mapplethorpe conversation remains unresolved. Black artists articulating their own relationship to this history is significant. Members interested in the critical history of Black representation in photography will find this valuable.
news.people: Black artists; Robert Mapplethorpe

news.title: Black Music Month 2026 begins at the National Museum African American Music
news.summary: NMAAM in Nashville launches a month-long Black Music Month celebration in June 2026.
news.detail: Black Music Month as a national institutional frame for Black musical heritage. Members who follow music and Black cultural institutions should know NMAAM exists and is active.
news.people: National Museum of African American Music; Nashville

news.title: Choreographer Jeremy Nedd explores viral dance at Lincoln Center
news.summary: Profile and interview with Black choreographer Jeremy Nedd on his work at Lincoln Center exploring the relationship between viral internet dance and concert dance.
news.detail: A Black choreographer taking vernacular digital culture seriously as choreographic material at a major institution. Strong conversation topic for Soirée members interested in contemporary dance and digital culture.
news.people: Jeremy Nedd; Lincoln Center

news.title: Save Harlem Now! is keeping historic preservation relevant
news.summary: Coverage of Save Harlem Now!, the historic preservation organization working to protect Harlem's cultural landmarks from development.
news.detail: Black cultural geography — the physical spaces where Black arts happened — is under active threat. Preservation is arts infrastructure. Relevant to Soirée members who care about the cultural landscape of Harlem and where arts institutions are housed.
news.people: Save Harlem Now!; Harlem community

news.title: Abdullah Ibrahim, quiet giant of the jazz piano, has died at 91
news.summary: South African jazz pianist and composer Abdullah Ibrahim, born Adolph Johannes Brand and previously known as Dollar Brand, died June 15 in Germany at 91. His composition "Mannenberg" became an anthem of the anti-apartheid movement. His final public performance was at the Cape Town International Jazz Festival in March 2026.
news.detail: Ibrahim was one of the great piano voices of the 20th century and a political artist whose work carried the weight of South African history. Soirée members who follow jazz and Black classical music should know this loss.
news.people: Abdullah Ibrahim

news.title: Abdullah Ibrahim, South African Jazz Legend Dies at 91
news.summary: OkayAfrica's obituary of Abdullah Ibrahim, framed through his South African legacy and Pan-African significance.
news.detail: OkayAfrica's framing gives the diaspora context that mainstream jazz coverage often misses. For members who follow the African diaspora specifically, this perspective matters.
news.people: Abdullah Ibrahim

news.title: Danny Simmons, founder of Rush Arts and passionate supporter of Black artists, has died at 72
news.summary: Abstract expressionist painter and arts organizer Danny Simmons died June 14 in Philadelphia at 72. Co-founder of Rush Philanthropic Arts Foundation with his brothers Russell and Rev Run Simmons. Co-creator of Def Poetry Jam on HBO.
news.detail: Simmons built infrastructure for Black artists and artists of color through funding, exhibition space, and media. His loss removes a significant organizational force from the Black arts ecosystem. For members who care about Black arts access and philanthropy, Danny Simmons built the systems that made access possible for many artists.
news.people: Danny Simmons; Rush Arts; Rush Philanthropic Arts Foundation
news.suggestedAction: Newsletter; share in week of his passing

news.title: Remembering Danny Simmons, founder of Rush Arts Philly and Def Jam Poetry
news.summary: Local Philadelphia perspective on Danny Simmons's legacy, focused on his founding of Rush Arts Philadelphia as a space for emerging artists.
news.detail: Shows the local/community dimension of Simmons's work beyond the national profile. Additional context for members interested in Black arts institutions in Philadelphia.
news.people: Danny Simmons; Rush Arts Philadelphia

news.title: Peabo Bryson Death: Pop/R&B Singer Was 75
news.summary: Grammy-winning R&B singer Robert "Peabo" Bryson died June 2 in Marietta, Georgia, from complications of a stroke at 75. Known for Disney duets "Beauty and the Beast" with Celine Dion and "A Whole New World" with Regina Belle.
news.detail: Bryson was one of R&B's defining vocalists across five decades, with crossover work that made his voice part of the American cultural memory. A significant Black voice has been lost.
news.people: Peabo Bryson

news.title: Peabo Bryson, Beloved Singer of 'Beauty and the Beast' and 'A Whole New World,' Dead at 75
news.summary: Rolling Stone's obituary covering Bryson's full career, from early soul recordings through his Grammy-winning collaborations.
news.detail: Broader career retrospective than the news-only coverage. For members who want the full picture.
news.people: Peabo Bryson

news.title: Peabo Bryson Dead: 'Beauty and the Beast' Singer Was 75
news.summary: Variety's obituary with focus on Bryson's entertainment industry impact.
news.detail: Industry trade perspective on Bryson's cultural and commercial legacy. Note for context.
news.people: Peabo Bryson

news.title: Turmoil at Dance Place in Washington, DC
news.summary: Tariq Darrell O'Meally, a Black choreographer who joined Dance Place as artistic director in June 2024, was informed his position was eliminated on May 28 via Google Meet. Executive director André Mazelin cited "dramatically contracting public funding environment." The organization will operate without an artistic director.
news.detail: A Black artistic director losing his position at a major dance institution, replaced by no one, is a story about what happens to Black arts leadership when funding collapses. Arts leadership stability matters for the kind of institutions Soirée partners with or directs members toward.
news.people: Tariq Darrell O'Meally; André Mazelin; Dance Place
news.suggestedAction: Monitor; flag for arts advocacy conversation

news.title: A New Lincoln Center Festival Puts Contemporary Dance Center Stage
news.summary: Lincoln Center launches the inaugural Pasculano Collaborative for Contemporary Dance, a biannual festival beginning June 18 with five international companies at Alice Tully Hall. Established from the largest single programming gift in Lincoln Center history.
news.detail: A new permanent home for contemporary dance at Lincoln Center signals institutional investment in the form. Soirée members who attend Lincoln Center events should know this new programming structure exists.
news.people: Lincoln Center; Pasculano Collaborative for Contemporary Dance

news.title: Your June 2026 Roster Roundup: Dancers and Directors on the Move
news.summary: Monthly roundup of ballet company appointments and departures. Includes South African-born principal dancer Siphesihle November leaving the National Ballet of Canada to join Dutch National Ballet as a soloist. Ballet West artistic director Adam Sklute to retire after 20 years.
news.detail: Tracks the movement of artists and directors through ballet companies globally, including Black dancers. Siphesihle November's move to the Netherlands is significant for a top-tier Black male ballet dancer.
news.people: Siphesihle November; Dutch National Ballet; National Ballet of Canada; Adam Sklute; Ballet West

news.title: BCALA Announces the 2026 Literary Awards Winners
news.summary: The Black Caucus of the American Library Association awarded the 2026 BCALA Literary Awards at the ALA Conference in Chicago. First Novelist Award to Addie E. Citchens for "Dominion: A Novel" (Farrar, Straus and Giroux), a southern family drama exploring patriarchy, devotion, violence, and destruction.
news.detail: The BCALA awards are among the most important recognitions specifically for Black literary work. A debut novelist recognized here often signals broader literary attention ahead. Soirée members who follow literature should know this author's name before the broader press does.
news.people: Addie E. Citchens; Black Caucus of the American Library Association; ALA Conference

news.title: Washington National Opera sues to force Kennedy Center to turn over $17M in gifts
news.summary: The Washington National Opera filed a federal lawsuit seeking $17 million in withheld donor gifts and endowment funds from the Kennedy Center after the two institutions ended a 15-year affiliation in January 2026. The Kennedy Center used a portion of the funds as collateral for a line of credit.
news.detail: A major American opera company suing the Kennedy Center over donor funds is an institutional crisis with direct implications for how federal cultural institutions are governed under Trump administration pressure. The structural collapse of the Kennedy Center under political pressure affects the entire performing arts ecosystem, including the pipeline for Black performing artists.
news.people: Washington National Opera; Kennedy Center
news.suggestedAction: Monitor closely; save for policy conversations

news.title: Washington National Opera sues Kennedy Center, alleging it withheld $17M
news.summary: Axios's reporting on the WNO lawsuit, with context on the Trump administration's role in the Kennedy Center's leadership changes.
news.detail: Axios frames the story through the political dimension — the WNO dispute is downstream of Trump's takeover of the Kennedy Center's board. The political context is essential for understanding why this is happening.
news.people: Washington National Opera; Kennedy Center; Trump administration

news.title: Kennedy Center judge orders tarp and programming update
news.summary: A federal court ordered the Kennedy Center to remove Trump's name from the building. Workers covered the signage with a tarpaulin after slow-walking compliance. The Center's calendar shows almost no programming. Artists have canceled appearances, citing politicization.
news.detail: The Kennedy Center is functionally non-operational as a performing arts institution. A court order about a tarpaulin is the visible symptom of a deeper institutional collapse. A hollowed-out Kennedy Center means fewer touring opportunities, fewer commissioning dollars, and less visibility for Black performing artists at a national stage.
news.people: Kennedy Center; Trump administration; federal court
news.suggestedAction: Monitor; save for policy and advocacy conversations

news.title: Conductor Slatkin, 81, and violinist Goosby, 29, talk concert music, golf, blues, politics and more
news.summary: Interview with Black violinist Randall Goosby, 29, discussing his musical roots in R&B, Motown, gospel, and classical music, and his connection to Black composers including Coleridge-Taylor Perkinson.
news.detail: A major young Black classical violinist on the connection between Black vernacular music and the classical canon — exactly the conversation Black classical artists are having in 2026. Members interested in Black classical music should know Randall Goosby's name and his framing of Black musical tradition.
news.people: Randall Goosby; Leonard Slatkin

news.title: Ailey returns to BAM under new artistic director
news.summary: Coverage of Alicia Graf Mack's first BAM season as Ailey's Artistic Director. The fourth AD in the company's 66-year history. The season features the return of Judith Jamison's Hymn for the first time in over 15 years.
news.detail: Graf Mack leading the company at BAM marks the beginning of a new artistic chapter at one of the most important Black dance institutions in the world. Ailey under new leadership is a significant institutional moment. Members who attend dance should know this context.
news.people: Alicia Graf Mack; Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater; BAM

news.title: Museum acquisitions round-up: a double-sided print by Kirchner and one of the most depicted Black models in pre-20th century art
news.summary: Monthly museum acquisitions roundup includes the Art Gallery of Ontario's acquisition of a painting featuring Pierre Louis Alexandre, described as one of the most depicted Black models in pre-20th century European art. The acquisition is framed through the museum's aim to represent "a more expansive history of Europe and the global interconnectedness of the African Diaspora."
news.detail: Museums recovering and acquiring work that places Black figures at the center of European art history, not its margins, is a long-term canon shift. For members interested in art history and museum collections, this acquisition type signals institutional repositioning.
news.people: Pierre Louis Alexandre; Art Gallery of Ontario

news.title: Schomburg Center in Harlem continues its centennial in 2026 with renewed purpose
news.summary: The Schomburg Center, which holds over 11 million items related to the Black experience, marks its 100th year with ongoing centennial programming, expanded access, and renewed institutional focus.
news.detail: A 100-year-old institution dedicated to Black knowledge and culture reaching this milestone deserves attention and celebration. The Schomburg is a resource Soirée members in Harlem and beyond should be using and supporting.
news.people: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture; New York Public Library

news.title: The Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture Is Turning 100
news.summary: Hyperallergic's centennial feature on the Schomburg, covering its founding, collection history, centennial programming, and significance as the primary archive of Black culture in the United States.
news.detail: Hyperallergic framing positions the Schomburg in the context of the contemporary art world and the canon debates of 2026. Members interested in archives, history, and Black cultural infrastructure will want to read this.
news.people: Schomburg Center; Arturo Schomburg; New York Public Library

news.title: Schomburg Center Turns 100 With an Art Historical Library Card
news.summary: A limited-edition library card was released featuring sculptor Houston Conwill's 1991 terrazzo installation "Rivers" at the Schomburg, under which Langston Hughes's ashes are interred.
news.detail: A library card as object connecting Langston Hughes, Houston Conwill, and the Schomburg's living collection is exactly the kind of detail that makes Black cultural history tangible. Members who collect or value Black cultural artifacts will find this meaningful.
news.people: Schomburg Center; Houston Conwill; Langston Hughes

news.title: Who's Afraid of Successful Black Artists?
news.summary: Analysis of four concurrent solo shows by Black artists at NYC's top museums in spring 2026, all represented by Hauser and Wirth. Examines whether the critical establishment is equipped to engage with Black artistic success at this scale without identity-flattening.
news.detail: This is not a show review — it is a structural critique of how the art world responds to Black artists at the market peak. Essential reading for Soirée's strategic positioning. Ebony can use this framing publicly.
news.people: Amy Sherald (Whitney); Rashid Johnson (Guggenheim); Jack Whitten (MoMA); Lorna Simpson (The Met); Hauser and Wirth

news.title: National Museum of African American History and Culture Opens Two Exhibitions Exploring the Power of Abstraction Across Art and Design
news.summary: "Revelation: A Journey into Abstraction" opens June 12 with 41 works by 38 African American artists from the NMAAHC permanent collection. Companion exhibition "Reset: Abstraction Embodied in Design" covers furniture, textiles, and lighting. Rizzoli Electa catalog available.
news.detail: The NMAAHC placing abstraction at the center of its exhibition program reframes the conversation about which traditions claim abstraction as their inheritance. Members interested in Black abstract art and the institutions that frame it should see this or order the catalog.
news.people: NMAAHC; 38 Black artists from the permanent collection

news.title: Three Fort Worth Black cultural institutions unite for Juneteenth celebrations
news.summary: The newly opened Fort Worth African American Museum, Kinfolk House, and the National Juneteenth Museum unite for Juneteenth programming. The Fort Worth African American Museum opened earlier in June with the inaugural exhibition "All 'N All: Artists Embracing Community."
news.detail: Three Black cultural institutions in the same city collaborating publicly on the same day signals a new kind of Black arts infrastructure in Fort Worth. Context for Soirée on how Black arts institutions are organizing beyond NYC.
news.people: Fort Worth African American Museum; Kinfolk House; National Juneteenth Museum

news.title: The transformative art of Maren Hassinger comes to Berkeley
news.summary: Feature on Maren Hassinger's retrospective "Living Moving Growing" at BAMPFA, which opened June 6 and runs through November 29. Her work spans sculpture, installation, video, and performance. Described as the largest retrospective of her work to date.
news.detail: A comprehensive reassessment of a major Black woman sculptor at a major museum signals where critical and market attention may move. Members who collect or follow sculpture should know Hassinger's name.
news.people: Maren Hassinger; BAMPFA

news.title: Whitney White Honored at 5th Annual Black Women on Broadway Awards
news.summary: Whitney White, Tony-nominated director of Liberation and Obie Award winner for Sustained Achievement in Directing, honored at the 5th Annual Black Women on Broadway Awards on June 1.
news.detail: Black women in theatre naming and honoring each other is significant. Whitney White is also a Black director with a genuine shot at breaking the Tony barrier for Best Direction of a Play. Members who follow theatre should know Whitney White's work and recognition.
news.people: Whitney White; Debra Martin Chase; Alana Raquel Bowers; Destiny Lilly

news.title: Classic FM's Rising Stars 2026: celebrating 30 inspiring classical musicians under 30
news.summary: Classic FM's annual Rising Stars list includes Black soprano Jazmine Saunders (Metropolitan Opera Lindemann Program, performing Clara in Porgy and Bess) and British violinist Braimah Kanneh-Mason. Single source for specific racial identifications — verify before sharing.
news.detail: Two Black classical musicians included in a high-profile European classical music outlet's under-30 list signals rising institutional recognition. Soirée members interested in young Black classical artists should know these names.
news.people: Jazmine Saunders; Braimah Kanneh-Mason; 28 others

news.title: As the Black Swan Musical Premieres, Dancer Ava Noble Takes Us Behind the Scenes
news.summary: Behind-the-scenes profile with dancer Ava Noble as the Black Swan musical, by Jen Silverman with score by Dave Malloy, premieres at Harvard's Loeb Drama Center. Note: Ava Noble's identity not confirmed Black through available sources — include with verification caveat.
news.detail: A dance-centered musical theatre piece premiering at a major university theater is an industry development worth watching. If Ava Noble is a Black dancer, this becomes directly relevant to Soirée. Verify before sharing.
news.people: Ava Noble; Black Swan (musical)

news.title: Playwrights Horizons Will Stage World Premieres From Aleshea Harris, Else Went, Kate Atwell, More in 2026–2027 Season
news.summary: Playwrights Horizons announces two Black playwrights in its 2026-27 season: Aleshea Harris ("Feast of Rabbits," directed by Harris) and Christina Anderson ("the ripple, the wave that carried me home," directed by Tiffany Nichole Greene). NOTE: announced May 28, four days before the research window.
news.detail: Both Aleshea Harris and Christina Anderson are among the most significant Black playwrights working in American theatre. Their presence in a major Off-Broadway season is a significant institutional endorsement. Members who follow theatre should know both names before the productions open.
news.people: Aleshea Harris; Christina Anderson; Playwrights Horizons

news.title: Blood in the Soil: Aleshea Harris Brings Play 'Feast of Rabbits' to Playwrights Horizons After Directorial Film Debut
news.summary: Blex Media's coverage of Aleshea Harris's upcoming Playwrights Horizons world premiere, with context on her directorial film debut and the political themes of the new play.
news.detail: Black press coverage of a Black playwright gives context that mainstream theatre journalism often skips. Members who care about Black literature and theatre will want to know Harris's new work is coming.
news.people: Aleshea Harris; Playwrights Horizons

news.title: Studio Museum in Harlem Announces 2026 Artist-in-Residence Cohort
news.summary: The Studio Museum in Harlem names its 2026 artist-in-residence cohort: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, and Taylor Simmons. Open Studios will allow public to preview work before September culminating exhibition.
news.detail: The Studio Museum's residency program has launched major careers. These three artists are worth knowing before the September show. Soirée members can meet these artists at Open Studios — this is exactly the kind of early access Soirée should facilitate.
news.people: Derriann Pharr; Simonette Quamina; Taylor Simmons
news.suggestedAction: Share; invite members to Open Studios

news.title: Schomburg Center, bastion of Black research and culture, celebrates 100 years
news.summary: amNewYork feature on the Schomburg Center's centennial, with focus on its founding, its collection of over 11 million items, and its significance for communities across New York.
news.detail: The Schomburg is not just a library. It is the archive of the Black world in America, and it is turning 100 in New York. Members who live in or near Harlem should be physically visiting this institution.
news.people: Schomburg Center; New York Public Library

news.title: The Schomburg Library is turning 100 this year — and throwing an epic rager
news.summary: Literary Hub's centennial feature with focus on the Schomburg's programming — Slick Rick hosting an old-school block party, family dinners from Arturo Schomburg's personal cookbook recipes, limited-edition library cards, author events.
news.detail: Literary Hub reaching a literary audience with the Schomburg centennial expands the institution's profile beyond arts-specific press. Members who follow literature and don't know the Schomburg's role in Black literary history will learn it here.
news.people: Schomburg Center; Slick Rick; Langston Hughes

news.title: Schomburg Marks Centennial With '100 Black Voices' Reading List and Renewed Mission
news.summary: The Schomburg releases a "100 Black Voices" reading list as part of its centennial, along with articulating its mission for its next century.
news.detail: A curated reading list from the world's foremost Black cultural archive is a concrete, shareable resource. Soirée members who love literature can use this reading list directly.
news.people: Schomburg Center

exhibitions.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
exhibitions.description: Photography by young Harlem residents placed in conversation with the Van Der Zee archive. A rare look at how Black youth document their own world.
exhibitions.artistFocus: 17 teen photographers, presented alongside James Van Der Zee archive photography

exhibitions.title: Long Gallery Harlem — Summer Exhibition
exhibitions.address: 2073 Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Blvd, Harlem
exhibitions.description: Long Gallery is one of Harlem's dedicated fine art galleries presenting work by artists of the African diaspora, including Bisa Butler, Derek Fordjour, and Alteronce Gumby. Exhibition running through July — verify current artist on site before visiting. Worth a stop on any Harlem arts day.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Artist not confirmed in current search — verify at gallery website before visiting

exhibitions.title: Ideas of Africa: Portraiture and Political Imagination
exhibitions.description: African and Afrodiasporic photographers examine Pan-African solidarity, portraiture, and political imagination across Central and West Africa. Closes July 25 — members have weeks left to see it. Keïta and Sidibé are canonical; seeing their work at MoMA alongside contemporary artists is a significant experience.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Jean Depara, Seydou Keïta, Malick Sidibé, Sanlé Sory, Njideka Akunyili-Crosby, Samuel Fosso, J.D. Okhai Ojeikere, Silvia Rosi

exhibitions.title: Ernest Cole: Black America Unseen
exhibitions.address: 23 East 67th Street, 2nd Floor, Upper East Side
exhibitions.through: June 18 – July 24, 2026. Tue–Fri 10 am–6 pm, Sat 11 am–4 pm.
exhibitions.description: Ernest Cole was a Black South African photographer who documented Black lives in America in the late 1960s and early 1970s — a rare body of work seeing its first New York presentation in decades. Closes July 24. Free gallery admission. Go before it closes.

exhibitions.title: Fade — The Sixth F Show
exhibitions.description: The sixth installment of the Studio Museum's F Show series — the most career-defining emerging artist survey for artists of African descent in the country. Seventeen artists, all with new commissions. This is where members see who's next.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Taj Poscé, Lola Ayisha Ogbara, Utē Petit, and 14 additional early-career artists of African and Afro-Latinx descent

exhibitions.title: From Now: A Collection in Context
exhibitions.description: Collection-based exhibition that frames the Studio Museum's holdings in conversation with contemporary questions about Black artistic life. Good anchor show for a first visit or a return visit.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Studio Museum permanent collection — artists of African descent

exhibitions.title: To Be A Place
exhibitions.description: Runs alongside From Now and the F Show. Specific works on view at the museum website.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Studio Museum permanent collection / special exhibition

exhibitions.title: MoCADA: Surrealism and Us — Caribbean and African Diasporic Artists since 1940
exhibitions.venue: MoCADA Culture Lab II — L10 Building
exhibitions.address: 300 Ashland Place, 2nd Floor, Fort Greene, Brooklyn
exhibitions.description: MoCADA is Brooklyn's only contemporary art museum dedicated to the African diaspora. "Surrealism and Us" traces Caribbean and Afrosurreal art from 1940 to now. Closes July 28 — last weeks to see it. One of the most overlooked cultural spaces in New York for Soirée members who haven't visited.
exhibitions.price: $11 general admission; discounts for students, seniors, EBT cardholders
exhibitions.artistFocus: Caribbean and African Diasporic artists, 1940 – present

exhibitions.title: Whitney Biennial 2026
exhibitions.description: The 82nd edition of the Whitney Biennial. Malcolm Peacock's work — 3,500 hand-braided strands of synthetic hair, with text by Douglass and Malcolm X — is among the standout pieces. Worth a visit for any member tracking the contemporary art world.
exhibitions.artistFocus: 56 artists and collectives including Malcolm Peacock

exhibitions.title: Firelei Báez: feet squelching on wet grass, nourished by uncertainty
exhibitions.description: Báez's first New York exhibition with Hauser & Wirth — new large-scale paintings, works on paper, and bronze sculptures across two floors. Colonial histories, Afrodiasporic memory, spiritual ecology, and the natural world. Closes July 31. Free and essential viewing for members interested in contemporary Black painting at the highest level.

exhibitions.title: Nicola Vassell Gallery: Follow Through
exhibitions.description: Nicola Vassell is a Black woman-owned gallery celebrating its fifth anniversary with a group exhibition featuring new and recent work by Adebunmi Gbadebo (Nigerian-American artist known for works that explore Black hair, memory, and ancestry) and Alvaro Barrington (Black British-Caribbean artist). A gallery whose founding mission is representation and inquiry. Free to visit.
exhibitions.artistFocus: Adebunmi Gbadebo, Alvaro Barrington (with Julia Chiang, Pam Glick, and others)

exhibitions.title: Sonia Boyce: Demonstrate
exhibitions.description: Dame Sonia Boyce CBE is a Black British artist whose work explores race, identity, and collective voice. "Demonstrate" transforms filmed encounters with ordinary people into an immersive installation of video, photography, and kaleidoscopic wallpaper — a meditation on voice as a vehicle for freedom. The Queens Museum is often undervisited by Manhattan-based members. Worth the trip to Flushing Meadows.
